tools.name: open_document
tools.summary: Open a .docx file into a session (Map sessionId->DocHandle, LRU 10 docs / 200MB / 30min idle evict).
tools.description: Open a .docx file into a session (Map sessionId->DocHandle, LRU 10 docs / 200MB / 30min idle evict). Returns {ok:true,sessionId,revision,summary,evicted} where evicted:string[] lists sessions dropped by the capacity cap to make room (re-open them if needed; later calls with an evicted id fail with E_SESSION plus a close_document remedy). Default summary is the full structural summary including the complete word/styles.xml dump (large templates return a large payload; no trim applied). Pass {"summaryOnly":true} for a palette-only summary ({palette:{availableStyles,brandColors,primaryFont}} parsed from word/styles.xml, no stylesXml dump). summaryOnly defaults to false (omitted/false keeps the full dump, unchanged, so existing clients never break). Example input {"path":"documents/report.docx"} -> {"ok":true,"sessionId":"sess_abc","revision":1,"evicted":[]}. Open first; keep the sessionId for every later call. Macro/active content refuses by default (E_VALIDATION naming the parts): pass {"allowMacros":true} to preserve or {"stripMacros":true} to strip (never both). Session ids are server-minted (sess_<uuid>, DEPRECATED to supply sessionId: client-supplied values are rejected with E_VALIDATION; deterministic ids are test-only via --allow-client-session-ids). IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: inspect_document
tools.summary: Inspect a session: standard TOON outline (fidelity compact|standard|full, default standard) plus style palette passthrough {availableStyles,brandColors,primaryFont} parsed from word/styles.xml, plus document core properties `metadata` {title,creator,subject,description,keywords,category,lastModifiedBy,revision,created,modified} read from docProps/core.xml (absent when the docx has no core part).
tools.description: Inspect a session: standard TOON outline (fidelity compact|standard|full, default standard) plus style palette passthrough {availableStyles,brandColors,primaryFont} parsed from word/styles.xml, plus document core properties `metadata` {title,creator,subject,description,keywords,category,lastModifiedBy,revision,created,modified} read from docProps/core.xml (absent when the docx has no core part). Renders the in-memory session state (includes unsaved execute_batch edits); `dirty:true` means the session differs from the last saved file, `revision` is the in-memory revision. Node ids are verbatim: paragraphs carry 8-hex w14:paraId (e.g. 3F2A9C1B), tables t_001.., sections sec_root, sec_2, sec_3.. by position; use them as-is for targets/anchors. A repeat paragraph sharing one native paraId reports a `<paraId>_dup` session id instead (e.g. 3F2A9C1B_dup): saving refuses until the repeat is deleted and its text reinserted for a fresh id. Tables render one row per table with grid cells as rNcM coordinates (r1c1 value | r1c2 value, rows joined by ;); merged spans are marked (spanN); merge covers are tagged hidden-cover (not directly editable, address the restart cell). Cell edits: the replace, style, namedStyle, clearFormat, hyperlink, bookmark and comment actions accept target "<tableId>:r<row>c<col>" (1-based, as the grid prints it; add ":p<n>" to pick one paragraph of a multi-paragraph cell). Other actions, including table, take the table id. Every row and column number counts from 1 (cell addresses, rowIndex, colIndex, columnIndex, row, col, index, afterIndex, fromRow/toRow/fromCol/toCol), so r3c2 and {rowIndex:3,colIndex:2} are the same cell. Chart nodes render style chart|chart3d with title + categories + series in the text ([Chart column] Title | cats: Q1,Q2 | ARR: 10,25), read from the chart part. Flag legend: [TBL] table [IMG] image/drawing [EQ] equation [CITE] citation [CMT] comment [TRK] tracked [LNK] link [BKMK] bookmark [L#] list level (1 is the top level; list ops count the same way) [+ADDED]/[~MODIFIED] diff; standard tier adds [B] bold [I] italic [C:hex] color [SZ:half-points] size [RS:name] run style [J:just] [N:num] numbering [HDR]/[ZEBRA] table look [CH:type]/[RID:id] chart. Palette lists every style id verbatim with no trim (large templates return the full list). 3-tier workflow for large docs: (1) macro-overview inspect (compact, first window) -> (2) search_content to find a target node id -> (3) local zoom via {aroundNode:"<id>",window:5} or page with {offset,limit}. Windowing opts: offset (min 0, default 0), limit (1-200, default 50), aroundNode + window (1-20, default 5) returning [node-w,node+w], maxTokens (200-8000, cuts on a clean row boundary, always reported via truncated/hasMore). aroundNode and offset/limit are mutually exclusive (use one or the other). Windowed renders preserve the requested tier; the TOON fidelity marker stays lossy by design (TOON is a lossy projection). Docs under ~2000 tokens return the full TOON (unchanged); larger docs default to the first ~50-node window {totalNodes,returnedNodes,offset,limit,hasMore,nextOffset,toonText} with a navigation remedy. Full fidelity requires sectionId; full-fidelity errors name the available section ids. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","fidelity":"standard"} -> TOON text + palette. Use the palette style names verbatim (e.g. Corporate Callout); never invent styles. When the session carries a style guide, the envelope also includes its compact styleGuide summary {name,headerFill,headerText,chartPalette,calloutTheme}. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: search_content
tools.summary: Search live paragraph/table w:t text; returns [{id,preview}] node hits for anchors/targets.
tools.description: Search live paragraph/table w:t text; returns [{id,preview}] node hits for anchors/targets. A table hit also lists `cells` (up to 5 addresses such as t_001:r3c1) for the cells that hold the match; pass one as the target of replace/style/namedStyle/clearFormat/hyperlink/bookmark/comment. Chart titles/series are NOT matched by search (they live in the chart part, not w:t); discover them in inspect TOON chart rows, then anchor by the chart node id. Image alt text and footnote/endnote bodies are NOT matched either (search covers body w:t text only); find images via inspect [IMG] rows and footnotes via their anchor ids. Search extension to those parts is a later-program candidate, not this surface. Default is an exact literal substring (case-insensitive); pass {"regex":true} to interpret the query as a regular expression (bounded: pattern <=200 chars, ~500ms evaluation budget, case-insensitive). Caps: first 50 hits, 120-char previews. Literal queries containing regex metacharacters return literal results plus a hint that regex:true exists. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","query":"Executive Summary"} -> {"ok":true,"matches":[{"id":"3F2A9C1B","preview":"Executive ..."}]}. Search before editing when the anchor id is unknown. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: execute_batch
tools.summary: Apply 1..500 strictly-typed operations atomically (strict discriminatedUnion per action; sequential:true default preserves document order; single edit = 1-item batch).
tools.description: Apply 1..500 strictly-typed operations atomically (strict discriminatedUnion per action; sequential:true default preserves document order; single edit = 1-item batch). Caps 500 ops / 200MB throw E_QUOTA with remedy (maxSteps is an optional positive integer, unbounded when omitted). Client-supplied op ids are honored where the schema allows (insert/equation/footnote/chart accept `id`; strict schemas reject it elsewhere). Style ops support word-level spans: `match` styles only the matched substring (run splitting; `matchAll` styles every occurrence, `matchCase:false` matches case-insensitively); an absent match fails with E_NOT_FOUND. Returns {ok:true,appliedCount,revision,skippedIds,createdNodeIds,results:[{index,action,createdNodeIds}],revisionsPending,revisionsRemedy?} where createdNodeIds lists new node ids in document order (use them as anchors in the next batch without re-inspecting). A batch that drops a non-empty redo stack signals it (redoCleared:true + redoClearedWarning naming the depth): a fresh edit invalidates redo, so redo_document afterwards reports an empty stack. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","operations":[{"action":"replace","target":"p_001","text":"Hello"}],"sequential":true} -> {"ok":true,"appliedCount":1,"revision":2}. On failure returns {ok:false,code,remedy} with a fix-and-retry hint. Image inserts take exactly one source: {action:"image",operation:"insert",anchor,fileData} for inline base64 bytes, or {action:"image",operation:"insert",anchor,filePath} for a file read from a directory jail (both together fail with E_VALIDATION). The jail resolves explicit allowedDir first, else the session anchor (dirname of the open document); outside-jail refs fail with E_SANDBOX, missing files with E_IO, oversize files with E_LIMIT; batch reads nothing otherwise. Callout themes (operations/callout.ts THEMES): indigo|emerald|amber|slate|rose (default indigo; unknown names render indigo). Optional styleGuide (bundled guide name or guide .md path, jailed like filePath: explicit allowedDir else the session anchor; remote URLs fail closed) overrides the session guide for this batch only; it never replaces or persists (to re-skin the session use compose_document with styleGuide). Omitted inherits the session guide. Guides cannot be detached: an empty styleGuide fails with E_VALIDATION; open a new session to work without a guide. Unknown names fail with E_VALIDATION naming the available set. Guide parse notes ride both server stderr and the client-visible warnings array. Layout operations: {action:"section",operation:"setColumns",columns,spacing,separator} (columns 1-12, spacing in twips, separator draws the dividing rule), {action:"section",operation:"split"|"merge",...}, and {action:"pageSetup",orientation:"portrait"|"landscape",paperSize:"A4"|"Letter"|"Legal"|"A3",marginTop,marginBottom,marginLeft,marginRight,columns,sectionIndex} (margins in twips and written as given, never rotated; orientation turns the page by swapping its width and height; sectionIndex counts sections from 1 and limits the change to one section, omit it to change every section). Section breaks: {action:"insert",type:"sectionBreak",anchor,position,breakType:"nextPage"|"continuous"|"evenPage"|"oddPage"|"nextColumn"}; the section before the break keeps the page setup and headers of the section it splits. Headers and footers: {action:"headerFooter",operation:"set",targetType:"header"|"footer",text,alignment,sectionIndex (from 1, default the first section)}; {PAGE} and {NUMPAGES} inside text become live page-number fields. Images: width and height are integers in EMU (914400 per inch, 12700 per point, 9525 per pixel at 96 dpi); give one and the other follows the image aspect ratio, give neither and the image keeps its own size fitted to the page. Tables created by insert type:"table" or by Markdown repeat their header row across pages by default. Equations: {action:"equation",operation:"insert"|"replace",latex,mode:"auto"|"latex"|"plain"}; LaTeX that contains a backslash, ^ or _ becomes a real Word equation, and mode:"plain" keeps the text exactly as written. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: save_document
tools.summary: Validate then persist the session docx (validator-gated save: throws E_VALIDATION with xPath + table/node location + remedy when the package is invalid, never writes corruption).
tools.description: Validate then persist the session docx (validator-gated save: throws E_VALIDATION with xPath + table/node location + remedy when the package is invalid, never writes corruption). Save-blocked remedies are xpath-specific (drawing docPr/id, table tbl/tr/tc, relationships, header/footer parts, session tracking-attribute leaks each name their own fix). Optional commit params: message (commit subject, single-line, max 500 chars; newlines become spaces; blank/omitted falls back to `save_document: rev <n> (<k> ops since last save)`); author (max 100 chars; blank/omitted falls back to ASTra Agent). Over-long message/author fail at the handler with E_VALIDATION plus a shorten-and-retry remedy (never a bare MCP -32602: caps are enforced in the handler, not the wire schema). A successful save clears the session dirty flag (revision is re-synced to the file on disk). The success envelope also carries revisionsPending (w:ins+w:del left in the saved package) plus a revisionsRemedy naming accept when >0. The success envelope also carries advisory changedValues [{nodeId,before,after}] (old saved text -> new live text, bounded: at most 20 entries, each side at most 200 chars, truncated flag honest; empty + reason when no baseline is computable). When the session carries a style guide (new_document/compose_document styleGuide), the envelope also carries advisory styleWarnings [{nodeId,rule,message}] (table contrast, chart duplicate colors, split-table orphans), never blocking. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc"} -> {"ok":true,"path":"documents/report.docx"}. Always save after execute_batch; close afterwards. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: close_document
tools.summary: Evict a session and release its lock/memory.
tools.description: Evict a session and release its lock/memory. Returns {ok:true,sessionId,dirty,discardedRevisions,warning?}: a dirty close warns (dirty:true + warning naming the discarded unsaved revision count) instead of silently discarding; save first when the warning matters. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc"} -> {"ok":true,"dirty":false,"discardedRevisions":0}. Close when finished; expired sessions (30min idle) must be re-opened. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: new_document
tools.summary: Create a new .docx from a template (report|memo|blank, default blank) at outPath inside an allowed directory (--allowed-dir / documents / system temp).
tools.description: Create a new .docx from a template (report|memo|blank, default blank) at outPath inside an allowed directory (--allowed-dir / documents / system temp). Validates the fresh package before writing (E_VALIDATION when invalid, never writes corruption); refuses to overwrite without {force:true} (E_CONFLICT). Success returns {ok:true,path,sessionId,revision,template,bytes} with the file opened into a session (use sessionId for inspect/execute_batch/save). Example {"outPath":"documents/new-report.docx","template":"report"}. Session ids are server-minted (sess_<uuid>, DEPRECATED to supply sessionId: client-supplied values are rejected with E_VALIDATION; deterministic ids are test-only via --allow-client-session-ids). IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions. Optional styleGuide (bundled guide name or guide .md path, jailed to the document folder; remote URLs fail closed) attaches a house style to the session at creation: later batches inherit its table/chart/callout defaults, inspect_document shows its compact summary, save_document reports advisory styleWarnings. Guides cannot be detached afterwards: open a new session to work without a guide. Unknown names fail with E_VALIDATION naming the available set.

tools.name: compose_document
tools.summary: Compose a Markdown string into the open session document (appends after existing content, except that a pristine blank template has its two seed placeholders replaced so output holds only composed content).
tools.description:
Compose a Markdown string into the open session document (appends after existing content, except that a pristine blank template has its two seed placeholders replaced so output holds only composed content). Runs the engine compose path, then applies the resulting operations through the same execute_batch path (strict schema gate, per-chunk quotas, structural checks, per-chunk atomic rollback, then inline-span run splitting), so every gate a batch meets applies here unchanged. Supported input: #/##/### headings (real Heading1..3 styles), blank-line paragraphs (single newlines join with a space), flat bullet (-, *, +) and ordered (1., 1)) lists with real numbering, GitHub-style tables with a header separator row (header row shaded and repeated), --- dividers, fenced or indented code blocks (monospace, line breaks kept), [^label] footnotes with definitions, inline spans (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, [text](url)) applied as runs with real hyperlink targets, and standalone block images/charts (![alt](path)) resolved from allowedDir. Out-of-scope input fails closed with E_VALIDATION plus a 1-based line number and writes nothing: raw HTML (except [!NOTE]-style alert callouts, which compile to callout containers), custom styles, general blockquotes, deeper headings, nested lists or tables, task items. Block image/chart refs need allowedDir pointing at the folder holding the files (refs stay jailed inside it; without allowedDir they fail closed); remote URL refs fail closed; inline data-URL block images bypass allowedDir by design (bytes decode in memory through the same image gates). Sources compiling past 500 operations apply as sequential 500-operation chunks; each chunk is atomic, but a later-chunk failure leaves earlier chunks applied (same exposure as any multi-batch caller). Compiled node ids are deterministic per source, so a second compose into the same session is rejected by the duplicate-id gate (compose once per session with the full source). Optional template (report|memo|blank) requires the open document to still hold that template seed, otherwise composition fails before any write (for a fresh templated document call new_document first, then compose_document with template), and placement is append after existing content except for the pristine blank replace above. Returns {ok:true,opCount,appliedCount,revision,createdNodeIds,results,validation:{valid,errorCount,errors}} where createdNodeIds lists new node ids in document order (use them as anchors without re-inspecting) and validation proves the post-compose package state via a read-only OOXML check (save_document re-gates before writing). A compose that drops a non-empty redo stack signals it (redoCleared:true + redoClearedWarning naming the depth): a fresh edit invalidates redo. Optional styleGuide (bundled guide name or guide .md path, jailed like image refs: explicit allowedDir else the session anchor; remote URLs fail closed) replaces the session guide (not a one-batch override: later batches inherit it until another compose replaces it) and skins this compose (table/header-fill, chart-palette, callout, and code defaults apply where ops omit params; explicit params still win). Guides cannot be detached: open a new session to work without a guide. With no guide, compose uses the built-in Default Corporate look (navy table header, bold white header text, striped rows). styleGuide "legacy" gives the older grey header for this call only and is not stored on the session. An italic-only line directly under the opening # title becomes the Subtitle; a [!NOTE]-style line outside a blockquote stays plain text and comes back in warnings. Later batches inherit it, inspect_document shows its compact summary, save_document reports advisory styleWarnings. Unknown names fail with E_VALIDATION naming the available set. Math: $$ ... $$ or \[ ... \] blocks become display equations and \(...\) becomes inline math (one line, up to 500 characters; refused inside links and table cells). Display blocks are top level only (inside a list item or alert body they fail closed). Optional dollarMath (default false) treats $...$ as inline math; off by default because prices and shell text can look like math. Workflow: open_document -> compose_document -> save_document. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","markdown":"# Plan

- a
- b
"} (add "allowedDir":"<dir>" for image/chart refs, "template":"report|memo|blank" to verify the seed). IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions. persistentIds maps each created paragraph id (md_0003) to the paragraph id the saved file carries, so a reopened session can be addressed with it (tables are renumbered t_001.. by position on reopen).

tools.name: export_document
tools.summary: Export the active document to HTML, Markdown, or PDF format with sandbox security gating.
tools.description: Export the active document to HTML, Markdown, or PDF format with sandbox security gating. Renders the in-memory session state (includes unsaved execute_batch edits, not the last saved file); success returns {ok:true,format,path|content,bytes,dirty,revision} (dirty:true = unsaved edits present). PDF renders via headless LibreOffice: a ~11s first-render cold start is expected behavior, not a bug. Failures return {ok:false,code,message,remedy}.

tools.name: visual_inspect
tools.summary: Inspect document visually with 2D spatial layout telemetry (ASCII wireframe, page breakdown, margins, defects) and optional headless rendered images (withVisual: true; add outputDir to write them to a folder inside the allowed directories, for example next to the document, instead of the server temp folder).
tools.description: Inspect document visually with 2D spatial layout telemetry (ASCII wireframe, page breakdown, margins, defects) and optional headless rendered images (withVisual: true; add outputDir to write them to a folder inside the allowed directories, for example next to the document, instead of the server temp folder). Renders the in-memory session state (includes unsaved execute_batch edits, not the last saved file); success returns {ok:true,sessionId,revision,dirty,telemetry,...} (dirty:true = unsaved edits present).

tools.name: get_document_history
tools.summary: List the saved git history for a session (newest first, read-only: never mutates, never flips dirty).
tools.description: List the saved git history for a session (newest first, read-only: never mutates, never flips dirty). Paginate with limit (1-100, default 20) and offset (default 0). Returns {ok:true,sessionId,documentPath,currentCommit,totalCommits,history:[{oid,message,author,timestamp,timestampMs,opCount,affectedNodeIds,resultingHeadOid}]} (timestampMs = ms-precision epoch millis; commit-time clock for tracked commits, git seconds for older ones; opCount is always present (0 for pre-tracking commits and heals-only saves: it folds operations, not normalizer rewrites); affectedNodeIds is always present ([] when untracked); resultingHeadOid always equals oid (append-only; refs never move). Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","limit":10} -> history slice. Use the oids with revert_document (or preview_revert first) to restore an earlier saved state. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions, and duplicate client-supplied ids are rejected. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: preview_revert
tools.summary: Read-only WOULD-restore preview for revert_document (never mutates: no revision bump, no disk write, no redo-stack change).
tools.description: Read-only WOULD-restore preview for revert_document (never mutates: no revision bump, no disk write, no redo-stack change). Target one commit: {steps:N} walks back N saved commits from the head (1 = the previous saved commit, must be < totalCommits) OR {commitOid:"<40-hex>"} jumps to that commit (mutually exclusive). Returns {ok:true,sessionId,targetOid,targetMessage,targetAuthor,stepsBack,affectedFiles,changedValues,changedValuesTruncated,changedValuesPositional,dirty,dirtyHandling,currentHeadOid,totalCommits} where affectedFiles lists package paths that differ from the target (word/document.xml plus tracked extras). The preview also carries advisory changedValues [{nodeId,before,after}] (live current text -> target restore text, bounded: at most 20 entries, each side at most 200 chars, truncated flag honest; changedValuesPositional:true means either side held orphan ids (no shared id across the boundary, common under duplicate native ids) so before/after pairing is positional, not identity; empty + changedValuesReason when the target range is not computable). Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","steps":1} -> preview summary. Preview first when a revert would discard unsaved edits. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.

tools.name: revert_document
tools.summary: Restore an earlier SAVED state as a new head commit (history is append-only; refs never move).
tools.description: Restore an earlier SAVED state as a new head commit (history is append-only; refs never move). Target one commit: {steps:N} walks back N saved commits from the head (1 = the previous saved commit, must be < totalCommits) OR {commitOid:"<40-hex>"} jumps to that commit (mutually exclusive). Bare reverts fail closed: unsaved execute_batch edits refuse with E_CONFLICT unless discardUnsaved:true, which discards them. The conflict remedy names net-zero edits (pending revisions count as dirty even when content matches) and carries dirtyReason with the pending count. Discarded unsaved edits are echoed back as {wasDirty,discardedNodeCount,discardedNodeIds} (counts + ids only, bounded), never silently dropped. Optional author (<=100 chars, default ASTra Agent) + reason (<=500 chars): when either is given the commit subject follows `Revert [N steps] to <oid> by <author>[: reason]`; otherwise the legacy `Revert to <oid>[: message]` shape is kept (message still accepted), and a bare default revert quotes the target commit message in the new subject (`Revert to <oid>: "<target message>"`). Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","steps":1} -> {ok:true,revertedToCommit,revision,dirty:false,discardedUnsaved,commitOid,commitMessage}. The pre-revert state is kept for redo_document. Selective middle-undo recipe (no cherry-pick: restore the older keeper, then re-apply the kept newer edits): 1) preview_revert the target, 2) revert_document to the older keeper commit, 3) inspect/search for fresh anchors (node ids die on every revert; never reuse pre-revert ids), 4) execute_batch to re-apply the kept newer edits, 5) save_document. Export-check after every mutation: run export_document (or inspect_document) after each revert and each re-apply and confirm the bytes before the next step. tools.description: Preflight read-only OOXML audit for a session: runs the same validator gate save_document enforces, before anything is written. tools.description: Ingest an on-disk Markdown file into the OPEN session (the file-ingress half compose_document lacks: compose takes an inline string only). Reads the file under the workspace jail, then runs the identical compose pipeline (strict compile gate, quotas, template-seed check, inline-span splitting), so the result is byte-equal to composing the same Markdown inline. sessionId is strictly required: the tool never auto-creates sessions (fresh templated document: new_document first, then import; existing file: open_document first, then import). Accepts .md/.markdown/.txt; .html/.htm refuse with E_VALIDATION (convert to Markdown first, same verdict as CLI import); .docx refuses with E_VALIDATION naming open_document (open .docx files directly). Optional allowedDir (image refs), template (report|memo|blank seed check), and styleGuide (same attach semantics as compose_document). Optional dollarMath (default false) treats $...$ as inline math; off by default because prices and shell text can look like math.
